clue.text: The bold-eat in a mess here — they have little choice

definitions.text: The bold-eat in a mess here — they have little choice

indicators.note: letters in a mess are jumbled up, so the words before them are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Brave diners in an army mess hall are given hardly any options for their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' signals an anagram of THE BOLD EAT; read as a whole, the clue also describes the set menu itself, where diners take what is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A set menu at a fixed price offers diners few or no alternatives, which is the whole sense of the clue.

clue.text: In fear, incline not to finish for a time

indicators.note: the shortened slope sits in the word for fear, so 'In' signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: awe is reverential fear

indicators.note: not allowing the word to finish means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a hill is an incline or slope

explanation.surface: Someone frightened is tempted not to complete a task for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means for a short period, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Bound to attract attention about the end of February

definitions.text: Bound to attract attention about the end of February

parts.words: Bound to attract attention about the end of February
parts.note: the clue suggests a jump made to catch the eye, but describes a calendar period notable for the extra day added at the close of the shortest month

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to draw notice around late February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it hints at a jump; the period in question gets an extra day, the 29th, at the end of February.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year adds a day to February, making the year noticeable for that extra date.

clue.text: It's carried by women -two women

parts.note: Dorothy is a woman's name
bag is a slang, unkind word for a woman, as in 'old bag'

explanation.surface: Something women carry turns out to be a pair of women.
explanation.walkthrough: The second woman is the disparaging slang 'old bag'. A DOROTHY BAG is a small drawstring handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned drawstring handbag hangs from the wrist, an accessory toted by ladies.

clue.text: See old boy put into play.

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to serve in tennis is to put the ball into play

explanation.surface: Watch as a former pupil is sent onto the stage or the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into play' suggests a stage production, but in tennis the serve puts the ball into play.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch or notice something is a simple synonym of seeing it.

clue.text: In my sleep I conceived a poem

indicators.note: the four letters sit inside the run of words that follows, so 'In' signals a word concealed there

explanation.surface: A dreamer says a poem came to them while asleep, like Coleridge's Kubla Khan.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is lurking across 'sleEP I Conceived'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem about heroic deeds, so it is one kind of verse.

clue.text: Carver lacking practical experience

definitions.meaning: a carver is a dining chair with arms, the one at the head of the table
an ... critic or expert theorises without hands-on knowledge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carver' suggests a sculptor or someone slicing the roast, but it is the furniture term for a dining chair with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver is a chair with arms, and an armchair general or critic is all theory with no field experience.

clue.text: Share, perhaps, in clothing

parts.note: taken as written
a vestment is a garment, especially a priest's robe

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a portion is perhaps included in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a share as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying shares in a company is one example of putting money to work for a return.

clue.text: Sponsor two men

parts.note: Pat is a man's name
Ron is another man's name

explanation.surface: A backer is supported by a pair of chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron supports an artist or cause financially, the role of a backer.

clue.text: The rates might provide these

indicators.note: the words could be made to provide a new word if their letters were reshuffled

explanation.surface: Local council taxes might pay for civic playhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might provide' tells you to rearrange THE RATES; the rates were British local property taxes, which could fund municipal playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Playhouses for drama were often run by councils from local taxes, so they are what the rates might fund.

clue.text: Ring for charming woman about 50 points ahead

indicators.note: the compass points go ahead of, before, the rest

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north

indicators.note: the enchantress's name goes around the numeral, so 'about' signals one piece placed around another

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who charmed Odysseus's men into pigs
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man looking for a delightful lady around fifty with an eye for points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' means casting spells: Circe the sorceress.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround it, as a verb of enclosing.

clue.text: Entertain a lot, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone throws plenty of parties, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' reads as 'much', but here it is one's lot, one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To fête someone is to honour them lavishly, hosting celebrations in their name.

clue.text: Make it easy for simple fellow to -. follow an exploit

indicators.note: the herb and the man come to follow, after, the deed

parts.note: a feat is an exploit or bold deed
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb
Ed is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone eases life for a naive man who must imitate a heroic deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like 'gullible', but as a noun it is a medicinal plant. To FEATHERBED is to pamper or cushion someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed someone is to pamper them, cushioning them from hardship as on soft bedding.

clue.text: Valentine cards may be kind

definitions.meaning: cards sent on 14 February usually carry a heart symbol
a plea to show mercy or compassion

explanation.walkthrough: The first part completes as a phrase: valentine cards may bear a heart picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic cards usually show the heart symbol, and the phrase is also a plea for mercy or sympathy.

clue.text: In variety act, I'd meant to make an entrance

indicators.note: something in variety takes different forms, so the letters that follow take a new order

explanation.surface: In a music-hall show, a performer intended to make a grand entrance on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' suggests music hall, but it is the anagram signal for ACT I'D MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Admittance is the right or act of entering, a synonym of an entrance.

clue.text: Assign an old teacher of law

parts.note: the article a
in the Bible the scribes were teachers of the Jewish law

explanation.surface: Someone designates a former law lecturer for a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old teacher of law' sounds like a retired professor, but refers to the scribes of the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to a source is to assign it, a synonym.

clue.text: Early wife?

parts.note: read 'Early' as 'earl-y', belonging to an earl: the spouse of a nobleman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' looks like 'first', but split it as earl-y: the wife of an earl holds this title.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl's wife holds the title equal to his rank in continental nobility.

clue.text: Baptise in foreign language after 1999

indicators.note: the language comes after the year

parts.note: in Roman numerals I before MM means one less than two thousand
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: A priest christens a child in an alien tongue at the end of the millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: IMM is an unorthodox but logical Roman 1999: I subtracted from MM. ERSE is Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism by total submersion in water means to dunk the person completely.

clue.text: A scent, you might say, to challenge the spirit

indicators.note: said out loud the word for a smell sounds like the French words

parts.note: an odour is a scent or smell
to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: A perfume, so to speak, that dares to take on the liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic English 'odour' sounds like the French 'eau de'. EAU DE VIE is brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for 'water of life', is brandy or another distilled fruit liquor.

clue.text: Soldier's mistake — there's a row about it

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the row goes around the error, so 'about' signals one piece placed around another

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A serviceman blunders, and a quarrel breaks out over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a tier of seats. A Terrier was a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A Terrier is slang for a volunteer in Britain's Territorial Army reserve, one kind of trooper.

clue.text: Someone staying out — guess he wants a change

indicators.note: the letters want a change of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor is out; guess he would like something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the definition, but it joins GUESS HE in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor lodging in a private home is a person stopping there temporarily.

clue.text: Uranium first discovered in this island

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
first is abbreviated 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A radioactive element was found on a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: UIST is an island of the Outer Hebrides, off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Uist names a pair of islands, North and South, in the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Caretaker in office (acting)

parts.note: Sext is one of the canonical offices, the prayers said at the sixth hour
on means working or in action, as a performer on stage

explanation.surface: A janitor is temporarily standing in at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'office' suggests a workplace, but it is a church service. A SEXTON looks after a church and graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton keeps a church building and churchyard in order, the parish's custodian.

clue.text: One who tells stories about one — a story-teller in reverse

indicators.note: the whole assembled word is to be read backwards
the narrator's word goes about, around, the numeral one

parts.note: a relater is one who relates, tells a story
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gossip passes on tales concerning someone, a narrator working backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside RELATER to give RELIATER, and 'in reverse' turns that round. To retail gossip is to pass it on.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to repeat it to others, so someone spreading gossip fits the sense.

clue.text: Advanced in fast time

definitions.meaning: the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' suggests speed, but it is fasting: the Christian season before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Money advanced is loaned, and the season of fasting before Easter carries this name.

clue.text: It could be naive not to make changes

indicators.note: the letters could be something else if rearranged, so they are an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone suggests it is foolish to refuse to make changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NAIVE NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To innovate is to introduce new methods or ideas, a synonym of altering things.

clue.text: Flag officer

definitions.meaning: a banner, especially one flown by a ship
the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy, or formerly a British infantry standard-bearer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag officer' is a real naval term for an admiral, which misleads; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a ship's banner, and also a junior commissioned rank.

clue.text: Bit of old opera

parts.note: the word completes both an old British coin, a 'bit' worth three old pence, and Brecht and Weill's 1928 opera

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bit' was a pre-decimal British coin worth three pence; the opera is by Brecht and Weill.
explanation.definitionFit: The pre-decimal three-pence coin was a 'bit', and Brecht and Weill titled their opera after the same amount.
